q: Monitoring confirms an active ransomware infection that is currently encrypting shares on a file server. According to incident management practice, what should the response team do FIRST?
c: Isolate the affected server from the network
Reimage the server and restore from backup
Identify and delete the malware executable
Notify regulators of a reportable breach

q: To avoid alerting on every single failed login, a security team configures monitoring to flag an account only after five failures within ten minutes. What is this preset threshold called?
c: A service level agreement
A clipping level
A baseline deviation
A false positive rate

q: A business unit states it can afford to lose at most one hour of data for its order system. Which recovery parameter does this requirement define, and what does it drive?
c: The recovery point objective, which drives backup and replication frequency
The recovery time objective, which drives how quickly service is restored
The maximum tolerable downtime, which drives recovery team staffing
The mean time between failures, which drives hardware replacement cycles

q: An organization exercises its disaster recovery plan by activating the alternate site and processing workloads there while production continues operating normally. Which test type is this?
c: A full interruption test
A tabletop exercise
A parallel test
A checklist review of the plan

q: A bank requires that initiating a wire transfer and approving it be performed by two different employees using separate credentials. Which operations principle is this?
c: Two-person integrity
Least privilege
Job rotation
Separation of duties

q: Before analyzing a seized disk, a forensic examiner duplicates it and records cryptographic hashes of both the original and the copy. What is the PRIMARY purpose of these steps?
c: To recover deleted files from unallocated space
To prove the analyzed copy is an unaltered equivalent of the original
To establish who owned the files on the disk
To satisfy chain-of-custody requirements by themselves

q: During an internal fraud investigation, an analyst collects a departing employee's laptop on Friday, keeps it in an unlocked desk drawer over the weekend, and delivers it to the forensics team on Monday. Defense counsel later challenges the evidence. What was the MOST significant failure?
c: Failing to image the laptop with a write blocker before it was placed in storage
Seizing the laptop without first obtaining a search warrant from a court
Storing the evidence in an unsecured location with no custody documentation
Not reporting the suspected fraud to law enforcement within a required timeframe

q: Corporate counsel informs the security operations manager that the organization has received notice of pending litigation involving a former business partner. What should the operations team do FIRST?
c: Suspend scheduled destruction and rotation of records related to the dispute
Forensically image every system used by employees named in the litigation
Verify whether the retention schedule already destroyed the disputed records
Export the relevant records and produce them to the opposing party's counsel

q: While reconstructing an intrusion, a SOC analyst finds that firewall, server, and application logs place the same events several minutes apart, making the attack sequence impossible to establish. Which control BEST prevents this problem in future investigations?
c: Enable debug-level logging on every network and server device
Aggregate all logs into a central SIEM repository for storage
Apply digital signatures to log files to protect their integrity
Synchronize every log source to a single authoritative NTP time source

q: Management is concerned that design engineers, who legitimately access proprietary CAD files daily, could send those files to a competitor. Which control MOST directly addresses this specific risk?
c: Full-disk encryption on all engineering workstations
A data loss prevention system inspecting outbound traffic for protected content
An intrusion detection sensor monitoring inbound network traffic
Quarterly recertification of engineers' access to the design file shares

q: A vulnerability scan reveals that dozens of production servers are running services that were explicitly disabled in the approved build image. Which practice would BEST detect this kind of deviation promptly in the future?
c: Annual penetration testing of the production server environment
Reviewing perimeter firewall rule sets during scheduled audits
Automated comparison of live system settings against the approved baseline
Requiring administrators to record manual changes in the ticketing system

q: An analyst holding a valid Secret clearance requests access to a Secret-classified project repository and is denied because she is not assigned to that project. Which security principle is being enforced?
c: Least privilege
Need to know
Separation of duties
Defense in depth

q: A warehouse manager has performed the inventory reconciliation process alone for six years; auditors eventually uncover a long-running theft scheme concealed through falsified counts. Which administrative control would MOST likely have surfaced the scheme earlier?
c: Mandatory rotation of personnel through the reconciliation duty
More rigorous background screening before warehouse staff are hired
Restricting the manager's system access under least privilege
Annual security awareness training for all warehouse personnel

q: An audit finds that 40 administrators hold standing domain-administrator rights, though each uses them only a few hours per month. The security manager wants to shrink the privileged attack surface without impeding operations. Which approach BEST balances these goals?
c: Have each administrator sign a privileged-account acceptable use agreement
Record and retain all privileged sessions for after-the-fact review
Require two administrators to act jointly for every domain-admin task
Issue domain-admin rights just-in-time and revoke them when the task ends

q: A financial firm is retiring self-encrypting solid-state drives that stored regulated customer data and intends to resell the drives to recover value. Which sanitization approach is MOST appropriate?
c: Overwrite every logical block on each drive with seven passes of random data
Perform a cryptographic erase on each drive and verify before release
Degauss each drive using a certified high-strength degausser
Delete the stored files and reformat each drive with a new file system

q: An organization exiting a public cloud provider must ensure sensitive data cannot later be recovered from the provider's storage, which the organization can neither physically access nor destroy. Which strategy BEST addresses data remanence in this situation?
c: Contractually oblige the provider to degauss the physical disks that held the data
Delete the storage volumes and let the provider reallocate the freed capacity
Encrypt all data before storing it and destroy the customer-held keys on exit
Overwrite each virtual volume with random data before deleting it

q: After a breach in which a service account with a weak, non-expiring password was abused, a nearly identical incident occurs two months later through a different service account configured the same way. Which incident management activity was MOST likely neglected?
c: Post-incident lessons learned and remediation follow-through
Containment of the systems affected by the first incident
Eradication of the first attacker's access and tooling
Detection and analysis of the original compromise

q: During an active data breach investigation, a journalist contacts a SOC analyst directly and asks for details about the compromise. How should the analyst BEST respond?
c: Share only details that the investigation has already confirmed as accurate
Deny that any security incident has taken place
Refer the journalist to the organization's designated communications contact
Offer to discuss the incident after the journalist signs a non-disclosure agreement

q: To reduce alert fatigue, a security operations center raises its intrusion detection thresholds until analyst alert volume drops by 70 percent. Which consequence should the security manager be MOST concerned about?
c: Analysts may lose proficiency at triaging large alert volumes
Real attacks may fall below the thresholds and go undetected
The sensors will consume more processing capacity evaluating traffic
The remaining alerts will contain a larger share of false positives

q: A security team deploys a passive honeypot that mimics a vulnerable database server in the DMZ, and legal counsel asks whether evidence it gathers could be challenged. Which statement BEST characterizes the honeypot's legal position?
c: It is enticement, which is generally lawful because intruders attack on their own initiative
It is entrapment, because the system was deliberately configured to appear vulnerable
It is unlawful interception, because attacker activity is recorded without consent
It is inadmissible hearsay, because the logs are machine-generated records

q: A critical vulnerability is discovered in a legacy manufacturing control system whose vendor no longer issues patches, and the system cannot be replaced for at least two years. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Formally accept the risk and document the decision until replacement
Remove the system from service until a replacement is procured
Apply an unofficial patch developed by the user community
Isolate the system on a restricted segment with compensating monitoring

q: A monthly vulnerability scan across 5,000 hosts returns thousands of findings rated critical by CVSS base score alone, but the remediation team can address only a small fraction each cycle. Which prioritization approach is MOST defensible?
c: Remediate in descending order of CVSS base score until resources run out
Rank findings by active exploitation in the wild and affected asset criticality
Fix the hosts carrying the greatest total number of findings first
Clear the oldest findings first to improve the average vulnerability age metric

q: At 2 a.m. a production database cluster fails, and the on-call engineer must apply an urgent configuration fix that would normally require change advisory board approval. Which action keeps the fix within a sound change management process?
c: Wait for the next scheduled change advisory board meeting before acting
Treat the fix as exempt from change management because it restores service
Apply the fix under the emergency change procedure with retrospective review
Rely on verbal concurrence from a peer engineer in place of a formal record

q: A change advisory board rejects an otherwise complete request to upgrade a core router; the implementation steps, schedule, and test results are all documented. Which missing element MOST likely caused the rejection?
c: A backout plan for restoring the previous configuration if the upgrade fails
Evidence that a vulnerability scan of the new firmware was completed
An updated network diagram reflecting the post-change topology
Written approval from the router vendor's technical support team

q: A team performs a full backup every Sunday night and an incremental backup every night Monday through Saturday. A server fails on Friday morning and must be restored to its Thursday-night state. Which restore sequence is required?
c: Restore Sunday's full backup followed by Thursday night's incremental only
Restore Thursday night's incremental backup by itself
Restore Sunday's full backup followed by Thursday night's differential
Restore Sunday's full backup, then each nightly incremental from Monday through Thursday in order

q: A company can tolerate up to 24 hours of downtime for its order-processing system but cannot justify the expense of a continuously synchronized alternate facility. Which recovery option BEST fits these constraints?
c: A hot site with continuously replicated data and standby systems
A warm site with installed hardware, activated with recently shipped backups
A cold site providing power, space, and network connectivity only
A reciprocal processing agreement with a nearby partner company

q: After a flood, a company operates from its hot site for six weeks while the primary data center is repaired. Repairs are now certified complete. Which approach to moving operations back to the primary facility is MOST appropriate?
c: Return the most critical business functions first to reduce hot site expenses
Return every function simultaneously over a weekend to shorten the transition
Return the least critical functions first to confirm the repaired facility is stable
Continue operating from the hot site permanently given its proven reliability

q: An organization has just completed writing its first disaster recovery plan and wants to begin validating it. Which type of test should the DR coordinator conduct FIRST?
c: A checklist and walkthrough review of the plan with the recovery teams
A simulation exercise built around a realistic disaster scenario
A parallel test processing live workloads at the alternate site
A full interruption test that fails over primary operations

q: During a business continuity tabletop exercise, participants find that the notification call tree lists managers who left the company over a year ago and cites a vendor contract that has been terminated. What does this finding MOST fundamentally indicate?
c: The call tree should be replaced by an automated mass notification platform
Exercises should be paused until the plan document is corrected
The coordinator failed to distribute the current version of the plan
Plan maintenance is not linked to the organization's HR and vendor change processes

q: An auditor at a data center observes employees holding the secured entrance door open for colleagues, including one person with no visible badge. Which control MOST directly prevents this practice?
c: Closed-circuit cameras recording everyone who enters the facility
A mantrap that admits one authenticated person per entry cycle
Stronger cryptography on the badge system's credential exchange
Prominent signage stating that holding the door open is prohibited

q: A bank wants night-shift security officers to be able to summon help if an intruder forces them to disable the alarm system at gunpoint, without the intruder realizing help has been called. Which control BEST meets this requirement?
c: A duress code that appears to comply while silently summoning help
A panic button mounted at the guard station
A two-person minimum staffing policy for the night shift
An audible alarm that sounds whenever the alarm system is disabled

q: A security analyst responds to an alert indicating that a production Linux server is actively communicating with a known command-and-control address. The server is still powered on, and a formal investigation is anticipated. According to the order of volatility, which evidence should the analyst collect FIRST?
c: A bit-for-bit forensic image of the server's hard disk drive
Archived authentication logs already stored on the central SIEM platform
The contents of system memory, including running processes and active network connections
Configuration files and scheduled tasks stored on the server's file system

q: Human resources asks the security team to pull email and badge records for an internal administrative investigation into suspected expense fraud by a mid-level employee. No criminal referral is currently planned. How should the security manager direct the evidence handling?
c: Apply forensically sound collection and documentation practices, because the matter could later escalate into civil or criminal proceedings
Collect the records informally, since administrative investigations only need to satisfy internal company policy standards
Refuse to provide any records until law enforcement first obtains a warrant authorizing the search of the employee's data
Withhold the records until human resources can demonstrate the employee's guilt beyond a reasonable doubt

q: During a breach review, investigators discover that a compromised domain administrator account was used to delete the security event logs on every server the attacker touched, leaving no record of the intrusion. Which control would BEST close this gap before a future incident?
c: Enable full-disk encryption on all servers that generate security event logs
Forward events in near real time to a centralized log platform where write and delete access is withheld from production administrators
Increase the local log retention period so entries are kept on each server for at least one year
Require administrators to review their own servers' logs each week and formally attest to their completeness

q: A financial firm's SOC failed to detect an intruder who logged in with a legitimate analyst's stolen credentials and gradually queried customer records for several weeks. Signature-based tools raised no alerts because no malware was ever used. Which capability would have been MOST likely to detect this activity?
c: An intrusion prevention system subscribed to an up-to-date attack signature feed
A vulnerability scanner performing weekly authenticated scans of the environment
Antivirus software with heuristic scanning enabled on the analyst's workstation
User and entity behavior analytics that baselines each account's normal access patterns

q: An operations team manually configures each new server, and audits keep finding inconsistent hardening settings across the fleet. What is the BEST way to ensure new servers start from a consistent, approved secure configuration?
c: Provision every new server from a maintained, security-approved standard image
Run a vulnerability scan on each server shortly after it has been deployed
Have a senior administrator peer review each manually built server before go-live
Record the approved settings in the configuration management database

q: During a critical incident, responders lost an hour because the configuration management database listed the wrong owner, wrong location, and outdated software versions for the affected system. Which improvement would BEST prevent a recurrence?
c: Launch a one-time data cleansing project to correct every record currently held in the CMDB
Restrict CMDB write access to a small dedicated data-quality team
Integrate automated discovery tooling and make CMDB updates a mandatory step in the change management process
Maintain a spreadsheet inventory as an independent backup to the CMDB records

q: A payment processor stores the master key components for its hardware security modules in a safe. Policy requires that no single employee ever be able to retrieve and load the key material alone. Which operational control implements this requirement?
c: Separation of duties between the key generation and key usage roles
Two-person control over opening the safe and performing the key-loading procedure
Job rotation among the staff responsible for cryptographic operations
Split knowledge implemented by issuing every custodian the complete key value

q: An internal audit finds that employees who transferred between departments over several years still hold access rights accumulated from every previous role. Which control MOST directly addresses this buildup of privileges?
c: Multifactor authentication enforced on all internal applications
Mandatory vacations for all employees holding sensitive positions
Role-based provisioning applied to all newly hired employees
Periodic access recertification with entitlement reviews triggered by role changes

q: A company's lease on twenty multifunction printers used by the legal and human resources departments is ending, and the vendor plans to refurbish and re-lease the devices. What should the security team require before the devices leave the building?
c: Sanitize, or remove and destroy, each device's internal storage in accordance with the organization's media sanitization policy
Delete all stored print and scan jobs from each device's operator control panel
Obtain the vendor's written assurance that all devices are wiped during the refurbishment process
Perform a factory reset of each device to clear its configuration settings

q: An organization rotates weekly backup tapes to an offsite storage facility using a third-party courier. Which control provides the BEST protection for the data if a tape is lost or stolen while in transit?
c: A signed chain-of-custody form accompanying every tape shipment
Selecting a courier service that offers GPS tracking of its delivery vehicles
Encrypting the backup data before the tapes ever leave the data center
Labeling each tape with its classification level and a return address

q: Responders confirm that a public web server was compromised through an unpatched content management system and that the attacker installed a web shell. The server has been isolated. What is the BEST approach to the eradication and recovery phases?
c: Delete the web shell file, run a full antivirus scan, and return the server to production
Rebuild the server from a trusted image, apply the missing patch, and restore verified clean content before reconnecting it
Restore the most recent nightly backup of the server and place it back into service
Keep the compromised server offline permanently and deploy a replacement with an identical configuration

q: During a suspected nation-state intrusion, the threat intelligence team wants to leave the attacker connected for several days to identify their objectives, while the operations team wants to disconnect the affected segment immediately. Both approaches carry significant consequences. Who should make this decision, and on what basis?
c: The SOC manager, because selecting containment tactics is fundamentally an operational security matter
The threat intelligence lead, because attribution evidence provides the highest long-term defensive value
The legal department, because rules governing evidence collection and admissibility override operational and business concerns
Senior management, because tolerating continued attacker presence is a business risk decision weighing intelligence value against potential damage

q: A retailer operates thousands of fixed-function point-of-sale terminals that run a small, unchanging set of applications. Malware has repeatedly evaded the terminals' signature-based antivirus. Which control is BEST suited to prevent unauthorized code from executing on these devices?
c: Application allowlisting that permits only the approved point-of-sale executables to run
More frequent antivirus signature updates pushed automatically to every terminal
A network intrusion detection sensor monitoring traffic on the point-of-sale VLAN
Full-disk encryption applied to each terminal's local storage media

q: A hospital plans to deploy an inline network intrusion prevention appliance in front of systems clinicians use for direct patient care. Leadership is concerned about what happens to care delivery if the appliance itself fails. Which deployment decision BEST reflects the organization's risk priorities?
c: Configure the appliance to fail closed so that no traffic can ever bypass security inspection
Deploy the sensor out of band in detection-only mode so that it can never influence clinical traffic
Configure the appliance to fail open, paired with redundant units and immediate alerting whenever inspection is bypassed
Postpone the deployment until the vendor can contractually guarantee the appliance will not fail

q: System owners complain that monthly vulnerability reports are full of findings that turn out not to exist, and remediation teams have begun ignoring the reports altogether. The scans are currently run without host credentials. What change would MOST improve the accuracy of the reports?
c: Replace the monthly scans with a single annual penetration test
Configure the scanner to authenticate to targets so it can directly verify installed software and patch levels
Filter the reports so that only critical severity findings are distributed
Run the same unauthenticated scan from several different network vantage points

q: A vendor releases a security patch rated critical for the database platform underlying an organization's revenue-generating order system. Exploitation has not yet been observed in the wild. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Deploy the patch to all production database servers immediately to eliminate the exposure
Defer the patch to the next quarterly maintenance window to avoid disrupting revenue operations
Rely on the vendor's regression testing and monitor community forums for reported problems
Test the patch in a representative staging environment, then deploy it through an expedited change with a rollback plan

q: A monitoring tool reveals that a senior engineer modified a production firewall rule two weeks ago without any change request. The modification fixed a genuine customer-facing problem and caused no outage. What is the BEST response by management?
c: Bring the modification under change control retroactively, review why the process was bypassed, and address the behavior according to policy
Revert the firewall rule immediately, because any unauthorized change must be undone regardless of its apparent benefit
Take no action, because the change was technically successful and clearly well-intentioned
Impose the maximum available disciplinary sanction to deter any future unauthorized changes across the team

q: A change advisory board spends most of its weekly meeting approving identical, low-risk activities such as routine certificate renewals and antivirus signature updates. What is the BEST way to streamline the process without losing control?
c: Exempt low-risk operational activities from the change management process entirely
Delegate all change approvals to the individual system administrators involved
Classify the recurring activities as pre-approved standard changes that are still logged and periodically reviewed
Combine the routine items into a single change request submitted once per quarter

q: To cut costs, an IT director proposes eliminating nightly backups for a file server because its storage array uses RAID 6 and can survive two simultaneous disk failures. What is the BEST response from the security manager?
c: Agree, because RAID 6 provides enough redundancy to make separate backups unnecessary
Object, because RAID protects against disk failure but not against deletion, corruption, or ransomware, which backups address
Agree, provided the array is first upgraded to RAID 10 for better performance and resilience
Object, because RAID rebuild times are too slow to satisfy the recovery time objective

q: A regional bank must be able to recover its core transaction database at an alternate site with no more than a few minutes of data loss. Synchronous storage replication between the sites was quoted far beyond the approved budget. Which strategy BEST meets the recovery point objective within the constraint?
c: Electronic vaulting that transmits the full database to the alternate site every night
Shipping encrypted backup tapes to the alternate site by courier each morning
Synchronous database mirroring over dedicated dark fiber leased between the two sites
Remote journaling that transmits transaction logs to the alternate site as they are written

q: A flood disabled a company's primary data center at 2 a.m. Recovery teams waited four hours to activate the alternate site because nobody on shift was sure whether the situation qualified as a disaster or who was authorized to say so. Which improvement to the disaster recovery plan is MOST important?
c: Define measurable disaster declaration criteria and delegate declaration authority to named roles with designated successors
Increase the alternate site's capacity so that it can absorb the entire production workload
Move the plan documents to an online portal that every employee can reach at any time
Schedule additional full-interruption tests of the alternate site every year

q: Regulators have asked a payment processor to demonstrate that its disaster recovery capability actually works, beyond the tabletop and parallel tests already performed. The DR manager proposes a full-interruption test. Which condition is MOST important before proceeding?
c: Notify the regulator in advance so that an examiner can observe the failover in person
Complete a fresh business impact analysis to reconfirm every recovery time objective before testing begins
Obtain senior management approval accepting the risk of a genuine outage, with restoration plans and low-impact scheduling agreed
Conduct the test unannounced to make the exercise conditions as realistic as possible

q: A newly hired business continuity manager learns the organization has no continuity program at all. An executive suggests immediately signing a contract for a commercial hot site to be safe. What should the continuity manager do FIRST?
c: Sign the hot site contract, since having some recovery capability is better than having none
Conduct a business impact analysis to identify critical processes and their maximum tolerable downtime
Develop and document detailed recovery procedures for the information technology department
Schedule a tabletop exercise to establish a performance baseline for the response teams

q: A company is designing fire suppression for a new data hall. Leadership's two stated concerns are protecting the staff who work inside the room and avoiding water damage to equipment from an accidental discharge. Which suppression design BEST fits these requirements?
c: A wet pipe sprinkler system, because water held charged in the pipes gives the fastest possible response
A carbon dioxide flooding system, because it suppresses fire without introducing any water at all
A deluge system, because opening every head at once guarantees complete coverage of the room
A pre-action system, which requires both detector activation and sprinkler head fusing before water is released

q: While reviewing data center emergency procedures, a security manager finds a step instructing operators to complete a graceful shutdown of critical servers before evacuating during a fire alarm. What is the MOST important revision?
c: Require personnel to evacuate immediately, because protecting human life takes priority over protecting systems and data
Streamline the shutdown script so the graceful shutdown completes more quickly
Allow operators to remain only when the fire is confirmed to be in a different zone of the building
Add a requirement to notify the incident commander before the shutdown begins

q: A regional retailer confirms that an external attacker stole customer payment card data. Executives ask the CISO to explain the implications of reporting the crime to law enforcement. Which outcome is the MOST accurate consequence of involving law enforcement in the investigation?
c: Legal liability for the breach transfers to the prosecuting agency once a report is filed
Internal investigators are relieved of strict evidence-handling requirements once police take over
The organization may lose control over the investigation's pace and the timing of public disclosure
Customer breach notifications become prohibited until the criminal case reaches a verdict

q: During a wrongful-termination lawsuit, opposing counsel challenges the admissibility of web proxy logs that show the former employee's repeated policy violations. Which factor BEST supports admitting the logs as evidence?
c: The logs were generated and retained as part of routine, documented business operations before any dispute arose
The log extracts were printed and signed by the CISO after the lawsuit was filed
The logs contain a complete copy of every packet the employee transmitted
The logs were reviewed only by personnel holding security clearances

q: A security operations manager wants twelve months of network traffic history available to scope future incidents, but the budget allows only a small fraction of the storage that full packet capture would require. Which approach BEST meets the investigative goal within the constraint?
c: Retain full packet captures, but only for the internet perimeter segment
Collect and retain NetFlow-style session metadata from all network segments
Raise SIEM alert thresholds so that fewer events are written to storage
Store full packet captures for one week and extrapolate older activity from that sample

q: A financial regulator requires that a firm's audit logs be protected from alteration for seven years, including alteration by the storage administrators who manage the archive. Which control BEST satisfies this requirement?
c: Hash each log file weekly and store the digests in a spreadsheet maintained by the administrators
Grant access to the archived logs only to the storage administration team
Compress and encrypt the archived logs using keys held by the SOC
Write archived logs to write-once, read-many (WORM) storage with enforced retention periods

q: A newly hired security engineer proposes applying a well-known industry hardening benchmark to all production servers exactly as published. As the operations manager, what is the BEST way to adopt the benchmark?
c: Tailor the benchmark to the environment, test it, and document approved deviations before enforcement
Apply every setting immediately, since the benchmark reflects industry-endorsed best practice
Apply the benchmark only to internet-facing servers, where hardening is actually required
Wait until the vendor incorporates the benchmark into a future OS release as default settings

q: A company is deploying its first fleet of Linux application servers. Operations wants to be able to detect and correct unauthorized changes to these systems later. What should be established FIRST?
c: A file integrity monitoring agent deployed on every server
A weekly vulnerability scanning schedule for the new fleet
A documented and approved secure configuration baseline for the server class
Verbose audit logging enabled on each server in the fleet

q: A software vendor's engineers routinely connect remotely with administrative rights to maintain a hospital's clinical application. Leadership wants individual accountability for every action the vendor's staff performs on the system. Which control BEST provides this?
c: Require the vendor to sign a nondisclosure and acceptable use agreement
Broker vendor access through a privileged access gateway that records each session under a named account
Issue the vendor team one shared administrator credential that is rotated after each use
Restrict vendor connections to business hours from allowlisted IP addresses

q: An operations director is negotiating a service-level agreement for a managed firewall service and wants a contractual commitment on how quickly the provider will restore the service after a failure. Which metric should the SLA specify?
c: Mean time between failures (MTBF)
Recovery point objective (RPO)
Annualized loss expectancy (ALE)
Mean time to repair (MTTR)

q: Legal counsel discovers that a business unit has kept every email and file share document for fifteen years 'just in case.' No litigation holds are in effect. From a risk management perspective, which practice is BEST?
c: Continue retaining everything, since more evidence can only help in future litigation
Immediately delete all data older than one year to cut storage costs
Enforce an approved retention schedule that destroys records once legal and business requirements lapse
Move all aged data into encrypted offline archives that are retained indefinitely

q: An organization stores hundreds of backup tapes in an onsite media room. Recently a tape needed for a restore could not be located, and nobody could establish who last handled it. Which practice BEST prevents a recurrence?
c: Operate a managed media library with labeling and a check-in/check-out log for every tape
Encrypt all tapes so that a lost tape cannot be read by an outsider
Replace the tapes with disk-based backups running on the same schedule
Move all tapes to an offsite vault serviced by a bonded courier

q: During response to a suspected compromise of the corporate identity provider, the incident commander must coordinate responders and brief executives, but investigators believe the attacker can read internal email and chat. What is the BEST way to coordinate the response?
c: Continue using corporate email but mark all incident messages as privileged and confidential
Move incident coordination to a predesignated out-of-band channel independent of the compromised environment
Suspend all response communication until the identity provider has been rebuilt
Limit updates to verbal executive briefings delivered only after the incident is fully resolved

q: A help desk receives two reports at the same time: a user's account is locked out, and a database administrator reports that customer records have appeared on a public paste site. Which incident management capability ensures the second report receives an appropriately urgent response?
c: A single queue that processes all tickets strictly in order of arrival
An annual tabletop exercise conducted with the response team
A root cause analysis procedure applied after each ticket is closed
A severity classification scheme that drives escalation paths and response-time targets

q: After eradicating malware and restoring servers from clean images, the response team believes an intrusion is over. Before declaring the incident closed, which step BEST reduces the risk that the attacker quietly regains their foothold?
c: Require all users to reset their passwords again every week for the next month
Archive the incident evidence and formally release the response team from duty
Apply a defined period of heightened monitoring on the restored systems for signs of residual access
Distribute the lessons-learned report to all staff without further delay

q: Threat intelligence identifies the command-and-control domains used by malware believed to have infected an unknown number of corporate endpoints. Which control BEST disrupts the malware's communication while also revealing which hosts are infected?
c: Block the malicious domains in the perimeter firewall's egress ruleset
Configure internal DNS to sinkhole the malicious domains and log which clients query them
Quarantine and reimage every endpoint in the organization as a precaution
Publish the indicator list and ask users to report any suspicious behavior

q: Signature-based email antivirus keeps missing malicious attachments used in targeted spear-phishing, because each campaign uses a freshly compiled, never-before-seen malware build. Which additional control BEST addresses this gap?
c: Detonate inbound attachments in an isolated sandbox and block those exhibiting malicious behavior
Increase the frequency of antivirus signature updates from daily to hourly
Configure the mail gateway to strip every attachment from inbound email company-wide
Route all email through a second signature-based engine from a different vendor

q: A vendor confirms a critical SQL injection flaw in its web application that a company hosts on premises, but the fix will not ship for sixty days. Taking the application offline is unacceptable to the business. Which action BEST reduces exposure in the interim?
c: Accept the risk and document the vendor's remediation timeline for the audit file
Modify the application's code directly to add input sanitization
Force all application users to change their passwords immediately
Deploy a web application firewall rule that blocks injection patterns targeting the flaw

q: The server team reports that last month's critical patches were successfully deployed to all systems through the patch management console. Which action BEST verifies that the vulnerabilities are actually remediated?
c: Review the deployment success report generated by the patch console
Close the findings, since the responsible team has confirmed completion
Rescan the affected systems and confirm the findings no longer appear
Wait for the next annual penetration test to attempt exploitation

q: A change advisory board reviews changes for scheduling conflicts and operational impact, but several approved changes later created security weaknesses, including a firewall rule that exposed a management interface to the internet. What is the BEST improvement to the change process?
c: Require the CISO to personally approve every change before implementation
Include a security impact analysis in the evaluation of each proposed change
Reduce the number of changes the board approves in each cycle
Run a vulnerability scan of the entire network after every CAB meeting

q: A payroll SaaS provider deploys platform updates on its own schedule, entirely outside the customer's change advisory board. The security manager worries that provider changes could break integrations or weaken configured controls. What is the BEST way to bring these changes under the organization's change management?
c: Subscribe to the provider's release notifications and assess and test upcoming changes in a sandbox tenant
Contractually require the provider to submit each platform update to the customer's CAB for approval
Declare the SaaS platform out of scope for change management because the provider owns it
Block the provider's updates at the corporate firewall until internal testing has completed

q: Two similarly sized insurance firms sign a reciprocal agreement to host each other's critical processing after a disaster, avoiding the cost of a commercial recovery site. Which issue is the MOST significant weakness of this strategy?
c: Neither firm can begin recovery until a disaster is formally declared by both parties
The travel distance between the two firms will slow the recovery team's arrival
Each firm must encrypt its data before processing it at the partner's site
The partner is unlikely to have spare capacity and compatible systems, and the arrangement is hard to test

q: A chemical fire forces evacuation of a processing facility, and the coordinator declares a disaster. All personnel are accounted for and emergency services have released the building back to the company. What should the recovery organization do FIRST?
c: Perform a damage assessment to decide whether to repair the primary site or activate the alternate site
Begin restoring the most critical business processes at the alternate site
Dispatch the salvage team to recover undamaged equipment for reuse
Notify the insurance carrier and begin documenting losses for the claim

q: During a structured disaster recovery exercise, the database failover did not work and the team badly missed the recovery time objective. Several executives call the exercise a failure and question the DR program's value. How should the DR manager BEST characterize the outcome?
c: The test failed and must be rerun immediately until the objectives are achieved
The results should stay within the DR team to avoid undermining executive confidence
The test succeeded in its purpose by exposing plan gaps that can be corrected before a real disaster
The recovery time objective should be lengthened so that future tests can meet it

q: A business impact analysis determines that the order-fulfillment process can survive at most 48 hours of outage before the company suffers unacceptable harm. The IT team proposes a recovery solution with a 72-hour recovery time objective because it is significantly cheaper. What is the MOST accurate assessment?
c: The proposal is acceptable because RTO and maximum tolerable downtime are independent metrics
The proposal is unacceptable because the RTO exceeds the maximum tolerable downtime set by the business
The proposal is acceptable if the recovery point objective is shortened to compensate for the longer RTO
The proposal is unacceptable because critical processes always require an RTO under 24 hours

q: An architect designing a new corporate campus wants the site itself to discourage intrusion: low landscaping that preserves clear sightlines, clearly marked transitions from public to private space, and courtyards that keep legitimate users present and observant throughout the day. Which physical security concept does this design apply?
c: Defense in depth
Deterrence through visible guard patrols
Target hardening with barriers and locks
Crime prevention through environmental design (CPTED)

q: A senior executive will travel to a country known for aggressive economic espionage, including hotel room intrusions and pervasive network surveillance. Which measure BEST protects corporate information during the trip?
c: Issue a clean loaner laptop and phone holding only the data needed for the trip, wiped on return
Have the executive carry the normal corporate laptop but avoid using hotel Wi-Fi
Rely on the corporate VPN to shield all of the executive's communications from monitoring
Instruct the executive to lock the laptop in the hotel room safe whenever leaving the room

q: An internal investigation confirms that a former contractor took proprietary pricing models to a competitor. Executive leadership decides to pursue a civil lawsuit for damages rather than refer the matter for criminal prosecution. What standard of proof will the organization's evidence MOST likely need to satisfy in court?
c: Beyond a reasonable doubt
Probable cause
Preponderance of the evidence
Clear and convincing evidence

q: A company is migrating its core applications to a SaaS provider. The security manager is concerned that if a breach occurs inside the provider's environment, the company will be unable to obtain the evidence needed to investigate. Which action BEST addresses this concern?
c: Negotiate contract clauses defining the provider's obligations for forensic support, log access, and evidence preservation
Prepare to issue a legal hold notice to the provider as soon as an incident is declared
Rely on the provider's most recent SOC 2 audit report as assurance that investigations will be supported
Install the company's own forensic collection agents on the provider's underlying infrastructure

q: During a walkthrough, a security manager finds an HVAC contractor working alone in the data center. The technician badged in on a visitor pass, but the assigned employee escort left to attend a meeting. Which control failure should the manager address FIRST?
c: The visitor badge did not restrict which internal doors the contractor could open
The requirement that visitors in sensitive areas remain under continuous escort was not enforced
The data center entrance lacked a mantrap to physically stop unauthorized entry
Camera footage of the data center floor was not being reviewed in real time

q: An auditor finds that a hospital's servers dutifully forward logs to a central repository, but nobody has examined them in over a year. A six-month-old compromise was discovered only when a third party reported stolen data. What is the BEST improvement?
c: Increase the log retention period so older events remain available to future investigators
Encrypt the central repository to protect the integrity of the stored events
Forward a second copy of the logs to a repository at the disaster recovery site
Implement automated alerting and a defined review process so logged events are analyzed in a timely manner

q: Customers repeatedly discover that a bank's online loan application is broken before the operations team does. During these outages, infrastructure dashboards show every server and service as healthy. Which monitoring approach BEST closes this gap?
c: Synthetic transactions that periodically execute the customer-facing workflow and alert when it fails
SNMP polling of server processor, memory, and disk utilization at much shorter intervals
Real user monitoring dashboards that the operations team reviews at the start of each shift
A network intrusion detection sensor tuned to recognize denial-of-service traffic against the web tier

q: To improve detection of malware and data exfiltration, the SOC proposes decrypting and inspecting all outbound TLS traffic, including employee webmail and personal banking sessions. Before deployment, which step should the security manager insist happen FIRST?
c: Load-test the inspection appliance to confirm it can sustain peak encrypted traffic volumes
Distribute the appliance's signing certificate to all managed endpoints to prevent browser trust errors
Obtain legal and privacy review and ensure employees are formally notified that encrypted traffic will be inspected
Configure exemption categories so personal banking and health sites are never decrypted

q: A SOC is deploying a SOAR platform. Analysts want playbooks to automatically disable any user account that triggers a phishing-related alert. The security manager approves automated enrichment and ticket creation but requires analyst approval before any account is disabled. What BEST justifies this decision?
c: Automation should never be used in security response because attackers can manipulate automated logic
High-impact containment actions triggered by false positives could disrupt the business, so they warrant human review while low-risk tasks are automated
Disabling user accounts is an identity management function that the SOC has no authority to perform
Playbook logic cannot be adequately tested, so any disruptive response step must remain fully manual

q: A new application server was built from the operating system vendor's default installation, which includes an FTP service, a web administration console, and several demonstration accounts that the application will never use. Which action BEST prepares the server for production?
c: Install the vendor's latest antivirus engine and signatures on the server
Place the server behind the perimeter firewall so the unused services cannot be reached from the internet
Remove or disable the unneeded services and accounts to reduce the server's attack surface
Enable verbose logging on the unused services so any attempt to abuse them is recorded

q: A cloud team defines its environments in infrastructure-as-code templates, yet audits keep finding security groups that were modified directly in the cloud console and are reflected in no template. Which approach BEST restores configuration control?
c: Run a nightly script that overwrites console-made changes with the template-defined settings
Require engineers to document any console change in the ticketing system within 24 hours
Take weekly snapshots of the environment so any modification can be traced to a date range
Restrict console write access and require all changes to flow through the version-controlled template pipeline with peer review

q: An accounts-payable supervisor has not taken a vacation in four years and insists on personally processing certain vendor payments even when workloads are rebalanced. Fraud examiners note this pattern as a classic red flag. Which operational control is specifically designed to expose schemes that depend on an employee's continuous presence?
c: Mandatory vacations
Job rotation
Separation of duties
Least privilege

q: A system administrator uses a single domain account with full administrative rights for everything, including reading email and browsing the web. A phishing payload executed in that session would immediately run with high privileges. What is the BEST corrective practice?
c: Require the administrator to change the account's password every 30 days
Issue a separate standard user account for daily work and reserve the privileged account for administrative tasks only
Add a second administrator so that no single person holds all of the administrative rights
Log every action performed under the administrative account for later review

q: An internal review finds hundreds of old virtual machine snapshots on a general-purpose file share readable by all IT staff. Several snapshots captured the running memory of database servers, including cached credentials and unencrypted patient records. What is the MOST important issue to address?
c: Snapshot sprawl is consuming expensive storage that should be reclaimed for production workloads
Snapshots are being used as an informal substitute for the organization's formal backup program
The hypervisor should compress and deduplicate old snapshots to shrink their storage footprint
Snapshots capturing memory and data must be classified, access-restricted, and retained like the sensitive systems they came from

q: A mid-sized firm's incident response plan assumes access to malware reverse-engineering and deep forensic skills that its three-person security team does not have. The CISO wants this capability gap closed before the next major incident. Which approach BEST addresses it during the preparation phase?
c: Send one analyst to an annual digital forensics certification course
Plan to competitively procure a specialist firm on the open market once an incident is declared
Establish a retainer with an external incident response firm that guarantees response times under pre-negotiated terms
Purchase a cyber insurance policy that transfers the financial impact of major incidents

q: Forensic analysis confirms attackers exfiltrated a customer database holding personal data of residents in several countries, and containment is complete. The response team wants to finish its full technical investigation, expected to take three weeks, before informing anyone outside the security department. Why should the incident manager reject this plan?
c: Breach notification laws in the affected jurisdictions may impose deadlines measured in days, so legal and privacy teams must be engaged immediately
The technical investigation must be handed to an external firm because internal findings are never admissible in court
Public disclosure within 24 hours is always required in order to preserve customer trust
The eradication phase cannot begin until senior executives have formally accepted the final investigation report

q: A security engineer notes that the organization's intrusion detection sensors flag only attacks matching published signatures, and a recent novel exploit passed through undetected. Which detection method is designed to identify such previously unknown attacks?
c: Signature-based detection with faster signature feed updates
Anomaly-based detection that flags deviations from an established traffic baseline
Reputation-based blocking of traffic from known malicious IP addresses
Stateful firewall inspection of connection establishment and teardown

q: An online retailer is installing an inline intrusion prevention system in front of its revenue-generating web platform. The vendor recommends enabling the complete blocking rule set immediately for maximum protection. Which deployment approach BEST balances protection against business risk?
c: Enable full blocking at once and rely on the vendor's default rules, which are tuned for typical e-commerce traffic
Deploy the sensor out of band permanently so that it can never interfere with legitimate customer transactions
Enable blocking only during off-peak hours until the operations team is comfortable with the technology
Run the system in detection-only mode first, tune the rules against observed traffic, then enable blocking incrementally

q: A vendor's download portal is offline, and an administrator finds the urgently needed firmware update for the company's firewalls on a third-party mirror site. The file name and version number match the vendor's security advisory. What should the administrator do BEFORE installing it?
c: Install it immediately because the advisory says the vulnerability is being actively exploited
Test it in the lab first, since successful operation there will prove the file is genuine
Verify the file's digital signature or vendor-published hash to confirm its authenticity
Scan the file with the corporate antivirus engine to rule out any tampering

q: During a quarterly assessment, an active vulnerability scan of a manufacturing plant's control network caused several programmable logic controllers to lock up and halted a production line. The security team still needs vulnerability visibility on that network. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
c: Use passive network monitoring and vendor-validated assessment methods designed for industrial control systems
Rerun the identical scan during a scheduled maintenance window so production is not affected
Exclude the control network from all future vulnerability assessments and formally accept the risk
Reduce the scanner's probe rate so the controllers receive packets more slowly

q: A retailer earns forty percent of its annual revenue during a six-week holiday period. In past years, infrastructure changes made in mid-November caused outages during peak shopping days. What is the BEST change management practice to adopt for this period?
c: Route every holiday-period change through the emergency change process so it is handled faster
Declare a change freeze for the peak season, permitting only emergency fixes under heightened approval
Keep normal CAB scheduling but require engineers to work extended support hours after each change
Delegate change approvals to individual system owners so decisions are made closer to the affected systems

q: A backup administrator reports a perfect record: every nightly backup job has completed successfully for two years. When a file server's disk array failed, the restore produced unreadable data and the files were permanently lost. What practice was MOST likely missing?
c: Storing a copy of the backup media at a secure offsite location
Encrypting the backup media to protect the confidentiality of its contents
Periodically restoring data from the backups to verify they are complete and usable
Running full backups every night instead of a mix of full and incremental backups

q: For resilience, a trading firm buys internet connectivity from two different carriers with automatic failover between them. A construction crew severs a single fiber conduit outside the building and both links drop simultaneously. What should the firm require when re-architecting its connectivity?
c: A third carrier so that the failover mechanism has more than one alternative path available
Higher-bandwidth circuits so that a single surviving link can carry the entire trading load
Stronger service level penalty clauses so the carriers compensate the firm for any outage
Verified physically diverse routing, including separate building entry points and independent last-mile paths

q: During a ransomware event that encrypted the corporate file servers and intranet, the recovery team discovered that the only copies of the disaster recovery plan and system runbooks were stored on the now-encrypted intranet portal. Which practice would have prevented this problem?
c: Maintaining current copies of the plan offline and at locations reachable during an outage, such as the alternate site
Exercising the disaster recovery plan through an annual full-interruption test of the primary site
Encrypting the stored disaster recovery plan so that attackers could not read its contents
Including the plan documents in the same backup sets as the servers they are written to recover

q: Six months after a successful parallel test of its disaster recovery plan, a company migrated its core applications from the tested data center to a cloud platform. Executives argue the plan is still current because the test passed so recently. What should the security manager tell them?
c: The plan remains valid until the next regularly scheduled annual test date arrives
The migration invalidated the tested procedures, so the plan must be updated and retested before it can be relied upon
Reviewing the previous test results in a tabletop session is sufficient because the applications themselves did not change
Cloud platforms remove the need for disaster recovery testing because the provider guarantees availability

q: A medical device maker's business continuity plan covers its own facilities and IT systems in depth. A fire at the sole supplier of a critical sterile component halts the maker's production for two months, an interruption the plan never contemplated. What weakness does this event BEST expose?
c: The plan should have included a reciprocal production agreement with a comparable manufacturer
The recovery time objective assigned to the production line was set higher than the business could tolerate
The business impact analysis failed to capture external supplier dependencies and single points of failure in the supply chain
The continuity plan was not exercised often enough to keep the response teams proficient

q: Human resources schedules the termination of a network engineer who has made veiled threats about taking the network down if fired. The engineer holds administrative credentials to core infrastructure. How should security operations BEST support this termination?
c: Closely monitor the engineer's accounts for thirty days following the termination meeting
Have the engineer hand over passwords and document configurations during a two-week notice period
Disable the engineer's accounts a week before the meeting so any problems can be found in advance
Coordinate with HR so all access is revoked at the moment of notification, with an escort and asset recovery immediately afterward

q: A security manager at a U.S.-headquartered firm is investigating suspected data theft by an employee based at the company's German subsidiary. The team wants to image the employee's workstation, export the mailbox, and send everything to U.S. investigators. What should the security manager do FIRST?
c: Image the workstation immediately to preserve evidence before the employee becomes aware
Request the evidence through a mutual legal assistance treaty between the two governments
Consult legal counsel on local privacy and cross-border data-transfer requirements before collecting anything
Obtain written authorization from the employee's direct manager to search company-owned equipment

q: During an internal fraud inquiry, an investigator must question a payroll clerk who is not a suspect but likely observed relevant activity. Which approach is MOST appropriate?
c: Conduct a non-accusatory interview with a second person present and document the statements offered
Conduct an interrogation designed to obtain an admission, since fraud occurred in her department
Have the clerk complete only a sworn written questionnaire to avoid face-to-face influence
Defer all questioning until law enforcement is engaged so police conduct every discussion

q: A SOC collects logs from firewalls, Windows servers, Linux hosts, and SaaS applications, but analysts cannot build cross-source correlation rules because each source records users, addresses, and actions with different formats and field names. All sources already use synchronized time. Which SIEM capability BEST resolves this?
c: Increasing log retention so analysts have a longer history available to search
Normalizing events from all sources into a common schema during ingestion
Forwarding all sources to a write-once storage tier to guarantee log integrity
Enabling verbose debug logging on every source to capture additional attributes

q: A CISO has received funding to build a security monitoring capability from scratch, and several vendors are already proposing SIEM platforms. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Select the SIEM platform with the broadest log-source support so no source is missed
Begin ingesting every available log source immediately to build a data lake for future analysis
Hire and train additional analysts so the platform is fully staffed on day one
Define the detection use cases — the threats, assets, and events that matter — and derive logging requirements from them

q: A company suffered a data exposure when a developer made a cloud storage bucket publicly readable. An internal review finds hundreds of cloud accounts whose configurations change daily with no oversight. Which control BEST prevents a recurrence at this scale?
c: Continuously evaluate cloud configurations against approved policy using automated posture management
Commission an annual penetration test covering the cloud environment
Encrypt all cloud-stored data using customer-managed encryption keys
Require all developers to complete annual secure cloud configuration training

q: A storage administrator asks who should decide the classification level and backup retention requirements for a new HR benefits database that the operations team will maintain. According to standard resource-protection roles, who makes this decision?
c: The storage administrator, as the data custodian who runs the backup jobs
The security manager, who writes the organization's security policies
The head of HR, as the owner accountable for the information
The database vendor, who best understands the platform's capabilities

q: A service desk keeps missing its four-hour customer commitment for restoring priority incidents because the internal network team, which handles most escalations, has no defined response times. Which mechanism BEST addresses this gap?
c: A stricter service level agreement negotiated with the customer
Operational level agreements defining the internal teams' response and resolution commitments
An underpinning contract executed with the internal network team
A memorandum of understanding between the CIO and the customer

q: An auditor finds backup cartridges containing regulated customer data stacked openly on an operator's desk. The operator explains that nothing on the cartridges indicated they were sensitive. Which control failure does this MOST directly indicate?
c: Backup media were not encrypted before being written
The media rotation and reuse schedule was not being followed
The cartridges were not stored offsite with a third-party vault provider
Media were not labeled with their classification to drive correct handling

q: A monitoring team logs thousands of routine events daily. Overnight it recorded: a successful scheduled backup, a user's single failed login followed by a success, a spike in messages blocked by the spam filter, and a database administrator account created outside change control that nobody recognizes. Which entry should be handled as a security incident?
c: The successful completion of the scheduled backup job
The unrecognized administrator account created outside change control
The single failed login attempt followed by a successful login
The spike in messages blocked by the spam filter

q: The help desk forwards a user's report that a 'hacker popup' appeared briefly on her workstation an hour ago. No monitoring alerts corroborate the report and the workstation is behaving normally. As the incident handler, what should you do FIRST?
c: Analyze the workstation and available telemetry to verify whether an incident actually occurred
Immediately disconnect the workstation from the network as a containment measure
Escalate to the CSIRT leader and formally declare a security incident
Reimage the workstation to eliminate any malware that may be present

q: More than 95% of traffic on a corporate network is now TLS-encrypted, and after a privacy review, legal counsel has prohibited bulk decryption of employee traffic. The network IDS detection rate has collapsed. What is the BEST way to restore threat-detection coverage?
c: Increase the frequency of network IDS signature updates
Deploy a TLS-inspection proxy to decrypt and inspect all user traffic
Deploy endpoint detection and response agents where content is processed after decryption
Block all outbound connections that the network IDS cannot classify

q: Visitors and contractors routinely plug personal laptops into live network jacks in conference rooms and reach the internal LAN. Staff need the rooms' wired connectivity for daily work. Which control BEST prevents unauthorized devices from joining the network?
c: Disabling all conference room network ports at the switch
Filtering by registered MAC address on each conference room switch port
Placing a network intrusion detection sensor on the conference room VLAN
Port-based network access control that authenticates each device before granting access

q: A critical remote-code-execution flaw is announced in an open-source library embedded in countless commercial and in-house products. The vulnerability team cannot say which of the organization's roughly 900 applications include the library. What should the organization do FIRST?
c: Apply the vendor's patch to every internet-facing server immediately
Query software inventories and component lists (SBOMs) to determine which applications contain the library
Deploy perimeter IPS signatures that block known exploit patterns for the flaw
Open an emergency change to upgrade the library in the next scheduled release

q: A vendor announces that the operating system running 200 branch-office servers will reach end of support in 14 months, after which no security patches will be issued. The servers currently receive patches normally. What is the BEST course of action?
c: Begin planning and budgeting the migration or replacement now, well before support ends
Wait until support ends and then isolate the servers on tightly segmented networks
Purchase extended support contracts from the vendor as the permanent strategy
Rely on the intrusion prevention system and antivirus to protect the servers after patches stop

q: An audit finds that changes are approved, implemented, and then closed automatically. Several changes later proved to have failed or introduced security regressions that went unnoticed for weeks. Which addition to the change process BEST addresses this?
c: Additional senior approvers on the change advisory board for high-risk changes
A documented backout plan required before any change can be approved
A post-implementation review verifying each change met its objective without adverse effects
Restricting all changes to a single monthly maintenance window

q: A change audit finds that application developers push their own code directly to production and approve their own change tickets 'to keep releases fast.' Management wants the risk reduced without abandoning frequent releases. What should the organization implement?
c: Full change advisory board review and approval of every production release
A rule permitting developers to deploy only during off-peak maintenance windows
Quarterly reviews of production deployments performed by internal audit
Pipeline-enforced separation of duties where an independent reviewer approves and the pipeline, not the author, deploys

q: Threat intelligence shows ransomware crews targeting the organization's industry now delete or encrypt online backup repositories before detonating. The organization's backups replicate continuously to a second disk repository that is reachable from the production domain. What is the BEST improvement?
c: Maintain backup copies that are offline or immutable and cannot be altered from the production environment
Increase backup frequency to reduce the amount of data at risk between jobs
Add a third continuously replicated online repository in another geographic region
Extend the backup retention period from thirty days to ninety days

q: A business impact analysis notes that only one engineer knows how to recover the firm's core storage arrays, and the recovery knowledge exists 'in his head.' He is nearing retirement. Which risk treatment BEST addresses this single point of failure?
c: Offering the engineer a retention bonus so he delays his retirement date
Cross-training additional staff and producing tested, documented recovery procedures
Purchasing a premium support contract with the storage vendor
Migrating the storage platform to a fully managed cloud storage service

q: A flood forces a company to run operations from its warm site. While the recovery team keeps critical systems running there, which team is responsible for repairing the damaged primary data center so normal operations can eventually return?
c: The incident response team
The emergency response team
The salvage team
The business continuity steering committee

q: After last year's disaster recovery exercise, the final report stated only that 'the test was successful.' During a real outage this year, recovery took three times longer than the business could tolerate. What should be added to future tests to make them meaningful?
c: Participation by every employee across the entire company
A full-interruption test conducted against the live production environment
Rotation of the exercise date so recovery teams cannot prepare in advance
Predefined, measurable success criteria tied to the business's RTO and RPO requirements

q: A newly appointed business continuity coordinator asks a consultant what single factor will MOST determine whether the continuity program succeeds across the organization. What is the best answer?
c: Visible senior management commitment to and sponsorship of the program
Selection of an industry-leading continuity planning software suite
The technical depth of the IT team's system recovery procedures
The number of continuity exercises the program schedules each year

q: A pandemic tabletop exercise reveals that all of the organization's continuity plans assume a facility or system loss with staff available to relocate; none address 40% of employees being simultaneously unavailable. Which improvement BEST addresses the exposed gap?
c: Contracting for a second fully equipped hot site farther from the headquarters campus
Extending plan scenarios to loss of workforce, including cross-training, succession, and remote-work provisions
Increasing system redundancy and automated failover across both existing data centers
Purchasing business interruption insurance that includes pandemic-related coverage

q: A company is replacing the decommissioned legacy suppression system in a continuously staffed, equipment-dense data center. Which fire suppression approach is MOST appropriate for this occupied room?
c: A wet-pipe sprinkler system charged with pressurized water at all times
A carbon dioxide total-flooding system covering the entire room
Handheld extinguishers positioned at each aisle as the sole suppression measure
A clean-agent gas system with pre-discharge alarms and an abort capability

q: An employee tells HR that a former partner has made violent threats and may appear at the office, and that she has obtained a protective order. What is the MOST appropriate organizational response?
c: Advise the employee that domestic disputes are personal matters outside the employer's responsibility
Circulate the individual's photograph and full details of the threats to all staff company-wide
Convene security, HR, and legal to assess the threat, brief front-desk staff on a need-to-know basis, and adjust access controls
Rely on the protective order and instruct the employee to call police if the individual appears on site

q: During a disaster recovery activation at the warm site, application teams restored their servers within their RTOs, yet the applications remained down for hours because directory services, DNS, and the storage network had not yet been recovered. Which plan improvement BEST prevents a recurrence?
c: Map application and infrastructure interdependencies and sequence recovery so foundational services restore first
Shorten every application's recovery time objective so restoration teams begin their work sooner
Assign additional staff to each of the application recovery teams
Replace the warm site arrangement with a fully provisioned hot site

q: A hospital's clinical systems must remain accessible even if the central identity provider fails, so the operations team maintains emergency 'break-glass' administrator accounts. An audit finds the accounts share one password known to the entire on-call team, and there is no record of when they were used. Which improvement should the security manager recommend?
c: Delete the break-glass accounts and require all emergency access to flow through the standard identity provider
Convert the accounts to just-in-time privileged access provisioned dynamically by the identity platform
Seal individually assigned credentials with a checkout process, alert on every use, and rotate each password after use
Require every on-call team member to sign an acceptable use agreement covering emergency account usage

q: During response to an ongoing intrusion, a senior engineer identifies the attacker's command-and-control server, finds an exploitable flaw on it, and proposes 'hacking back' to delete the company's stolen data before it spreads. What is the MOST appropriate position for the incident response manager to take?
c: Reject the proposal because accessing systems the organization does not own is unlawful, and continue containment while referring attacker details to law enforcement
Approve the action but restrict it to deleting only the organization's own stolen files from the attacker's server
Approve the action if legal counsel documents that the attacker struck first, establishing a self-defense justification
Reject the proposal because the server is likely a compromised third-party host, but permit the action if the engineer confirms the attacker owns the infrastructure

q: An audit of a perimeter firewall finds dozens of overly permissive rules, including several 'temporary' any-to-any entries created years ago for troubleshooting and never removed. Which practice would BEST prevent this condition from recurring?
c: Migrate the perimeter to a next-generation firewall that inspects traffic at the application layer
Periodic rule-base reviews that recertify each rule against a documented business justification, with automatic expiry dates on temporary rules
Configure the firewall to log all permitted connections and forward the logs to the SIEM for analysis
Restrict firewall administration rights to a single senior engineer to ensure consistent rule hygiene

q: A small firm stores every nightly backup on a NAS appliance located in the same server room as the systems it protects. A consultant warns that a single fire or theft could destroy both production data and all backups. Which recommendation BEST addresses this risk?
c: Increase the backup frequency so that more restore points accumulate on the NAS appliance
Enable filesystem snapshots on the NAS to provide faster point-in-time recovery options
Encrypt all backup data stored on the NAS appliance using strong cryptography
Maintain multiple backup copies on different media, with at least one copy stored at an offsite location

q: After the IT department completes and successfully tests a disaster recovery plan covering all data-center systems, the CIO reports to the board that the company is now 'fully prepared for any disruption.' Why should the CISO challenge this claim?
c: Disaster recovery restores IT services only; continuity of the business also depends on plans for personnel, workspace, suppliers, and manual workarounds for critical processes
No preparedness claim is valid until the plan has been proven in a full-interruption exercise rather than lesser test types
The test results must first be validated against board-approved recovery time objectives before success can be reported upward
Declaring organizational readiness is the prerogative of the business continuity steering committee, not the CIO
